text:
Tom Wilson hasn't scored in 16 games, and the Capitals have noticed the hole. He scored 30 goals last season; this year he has 2 on 5.9 expected, shooting 5.9% against a range we'd put between 12% and 17%. Over his last ten games he has two assists and his ice time has slipped by almost two minutes.

The underlying game hasn't collapsed. Washington takes about 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, he still gets to the dangerous areas at roughly a goal every 60 minutes of chances, and he's still doing the physical stuff, with 54 hits. Evolving-Hockey rated him 58th among forwards last season and at the 99th percentile for taking chances away, and noted that even then his goals trailed his chances.

He also dropped the gloves off the opening faceoff against Buffalo on Nov. 19, the kind of night that says a lot about how he's trying to drag a team out of a slide. The drought looks like finishing luck. What we'd watch is whether the minutes come back before the goals do.
headline: Tom Wilson's goals have gone missing, not his chances
